title: Savings & Money Market Accounts: why an excess withdrawal fee on a certificate funding transfer is a bank error
content:
## Scope

This rule applies to a Savings & Money Market Accounts account from which the owner opened a certificate of deposit by internal transfer, where an excess withdrawal fee was charged on that transfer. It decides, from the tier's list of counted channels, whether the fee is refunded.

## Policy clause

An internal transfer from a savings account that opens a certificate of deposit of the same owner is posted as an internal transfer. An internal transfer is never one of the tier's counted withdrawal channels, so an excess withdrawal fee charged on that transfer was assessed contrary to the charter and is refunded in full as a bank-error refund.

When the tier's counted channels do list internal transfers, nothing is refunded under this rule.

## Truth table

| Tier's counted channels include internal transfers | Excess withdrawal fee attached to the funding transfer | Under this rule |
|---|---|---|
| no | yes | the fee is refunded in full as a bank error |
| no | no | nothing to refund |
| yes | any | nothing is refunded |

## Reasoning chain, as the rule states it

Funding transfer posted as an internal transfer, then internal transfer never on the tier's counted list, then the excess withdrawal fee on it assessed contrary to the charter, then a refund of that fee in full on the bank-error ground.

## Points of judgement

**Wrong reading:** "The customer had already used the cycle's allowance, so the fee on the certificate funding transfer stands." **Correct basis:** the allowance position is irrelevant; the transfer was never a counted withdrawal.

**Wrong reading:** "Refund it as a courtesy." **Correct basis:** the fee was assessed contrary to the charter, so the ground is bank error.
